chunks: From him, from Hārūn ibn Muslim, from Masʿadah ibn Ziyād, from Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said:

My father, may Allah be pleased with him, used to do this: when the claimant group did not swear along with the evidence regarding the killing of their slain person, and they did not swear that the accused had killed him, he would make the accused swear fifty oaths concerning the killing: “By Allah, we did not kill him, nor do we know any killer for him.” Then the blood-money is paid to the heirs of the slain. That is when he is killed within a single clan.
But if he is killed in a military camp or in the market of a city, then his blood-money is paid to his heirs from the public treasury.

key_terms.أَوْلِيَاءِ الْقَتِيلِ: the heirs or legal guardians of the slain person
key_terms.الْمُدَّعُونَ: the claimants who bring the accusation
key_terms.خَمْسِينَ يَمِينًا: fifty legal oaths sworn in the case

ai.seo_question: How is diyah handled in Shia fiqh when the killer of a slain person is unknown?
ai.summary: This hadith explains a legal ruling concerning an unidentified killer and the procedure of oaths and blood-money. It distinguishes between a killing occurring within a single clan, where the accused swear oaths and the diyah is paid to the heirs, and a killing in a public setting, where the diyah is paid from the bayt al-mal.
